answer: A sybil can mint a flock of sparrow-light identities overnight, but each must earn non-transferable reputation that only hardens like a crystal over many epochs of peer-verified work. Reputation cannot be bought or moved between accounts; it stains each one like pigment that fades without continuous honest activity. To fake N trusted agents the attacker must fund and keep all N busy for the full ripening time, so cost scales linearly per head while one honest agent pays the ripening cost just once.
